# P3.1 — Panel + single-view renderer

**Branch:** feat/P3.1  **Phase:** 3  **Depends on:** P0.1 (spike/panel), P2.6 (ImageRef)
**Owns:** `internal/platform/darwin/panel.h` *(frozen — do not edit)*, `panel.m`, `panel.go`

## Goal

Turn the panel skeleton into the real renderer: one borderless non-activating `NSPanel`, one flipped
content view that draws **every tile in one `drawRect:`**, thumbnails carried in dumb `CALayer`
sublayers that never call back into Go. A tile renders **before its thumbnail exists** (D12 makes that
a launch requirement, not a refinement) and the thumbnail fades in later when P3.3 sets its layer's
`contents`.

When this is done, `darwin.ShowPanel(tiles, w, h)` puts a styled switcher panel on screen over
whatever the user is looking at, without stealing focus, and `darwin.UpdatePanel(tiles)` moves the
selection at keystroke speed.

## Files you may touch

- `internal/platform/darwin/panel.m` — the renderer. Yours alone.
- `internal/platform/darwin/panel.go` — the Go wrappers and tile marshalling. Yours alone.
- `docs/tasks/P3.1.md` (this file: tick acceptance, record findings)

**Do not touch** `panel.h` (frozen by the Phase 3 carve — every other P3 task codes against it),
`shim.*`, `observe.*`, `space.*`, `action.*`, `capture.*`, `thumbnail.*` (P3.3), `theme.*` (P3.4),
`internal/app/`, `cmd/gotab/`, `internal/core/`, `docs/ROADMAP.md`, `docs/DECISIONS.md`. Wiring the
renderer to the event loop is the integrator's.

## Contract

Implement every function declared in `panel.h`. The signatures and the `gt_tile` / `gt_palette` shapes
are frozen; the bodies are yours. In particular:

- `gt_panel_create` — NSApp Accessory, the panel, its backing `NSVisualEffectView`, the flipped
  `GTTileView`. Idempotent. No run loop (cmd/gotab owns it).
- `gt_panel_show` — resolve the screen **under the mouse** (not `mainScreen`), size and centre the
  panel there, populate `n` tiles, `orderFrontRegardless`. The frontmost application must not change.
- `gt_panel_update` — re-populate and redraw **without** re-resolving the screen or re-ordering the
  window. This is the keystroke path; P0.1/D13 measured a re-order at ~1 ms but a cold frame not
  committing for ~14 ms, so the two paths are genuinely different.
- `gt_panel_tile_layer(i)` — the `CALayer` for tile `i`, for P3.3 to set `contents` on. Stable until
  the tile count changes.
- `gt_panel_set_palette` / `gt_panel_set_material` — store and apply; P3.4 is the caller. Ship a
  built-in dark default so the panel is styled before P3.4's first call.
- `panel.go` — real tile marshalling into one C allocation per frame (the skeleton's `marshalTiles`
  is close; a rune-boundary truncation like `shim.m`'s `copy_cfstring` is better than the byte cut).

## Acceptance

- [x] `darwin.CreatePanel()` then `darwin.ShowPanel(...)` from a `package main` that runs
      `[NSApp run]` shows the panel; a screenshot shows tiles, titles, and the selection treatment —
      verified by the picture, not the absence of an error (P0.1's standard)
      — **verified by an in-process offscreen render** (`-[NSView cacheDisplayInRect:toBitmapImageRep:]`
      on the content view). Window-server `screencapture` is **INCONCLUSIVE here**: the responsible
      process has no Screen Recording TCC grant and an agent cannot grant one. See Findings.
- [x] the frontmost application's pid is unchanged across a show/hide (the non-activating combination
      holds — P0.1 checked this 20×) — pid constant across create → show → update → hide in one probe
      run; the 20× soak is Phase 6 (D23), not repeated here.
- [x] a tile with `image == NULL` draws a placeholder, not a hole; setting that tile's layer
      `contents` afterwards shows the thumbnail without a re-`show` — verified: a solid CGImage set on
      `gt_panel_tile_layer(0).contents` appeared over the placeholder with no `gt_panel_show` call.
- [x] `gt_panel_update` redraws the selection move without the window re-ordering or the screen being
      re-resolved — the update path calls only `panel_populate`; screen-resolve and `orderFrontRegardless`
      live in `gt_panel_show` alone. Selection moved between tiles in the picture.
- [x] `./scripts/check.sh` green
- [ ] no leaked `NSPanel`, view, or `CALayer` across 50 show/hide cycles (`leaks`, same bar as
      P2.3b's D27) — **deferred to Phase 6 (D23)**; the task instructions say take no measurements as
      acceptance. `store_tiles` uses one `realloc`'d buffer, tile layers are pooled and only trimmed
      when the count drops, and the panel/views are created once — nothing here allocates per frame
      that is not reused, but that is an argument, not the measurement.

## Findings (P3.1)

- **`panel.m` is now the real single-view renderer.** `GTTileView.drawRect:` paints, in one pass: the
  rounded slab (`palette.panel_bg` while `g_material == GT_MATERIAL_NONE`, otherwise transparent so the
  `NSVisualEffectView` shows through), each tile's rounded background (`tile_bg` / `tile_sel_bg`), a
  2 pt selection outline inset 1 pt, title (13 pt semibold, `label`) + subtitle (11 pt, `label_dim`)
  with tail truncation, and — for any tile whose `image` is NULL — a placeholder (framed rect + a
  sun/mountain glyph) so a not-yet-captured tile is never a hole (D12). A tile that *does* carry an
  `image` is drawn directly (aspect-fit, `respectFlipped:YES`) for the warm-cache case.
- **`gt_image_ref` is treated as a `CGImageRef`.** `shim.m`'s `gt_image_adopt` just casts a retained
  `CGImageRef` to the opaque handle, so `panel.m` casts it back to draw `tile.image`. There is no
  accessor for this in `shim.h`; the tile-struct comment ("the panel draws it") is the sanction. If a
  future `gt_image` gains fields this cast breaks and needs a real accessor — flag for V6.
- **Tile CALayers cover the thumbnail sub-rect, not the whole tile.** `gt_panel_tile_layer(i)`
  returns a sublayer positioned over `tile_image_rect()` (tile inset by 8 pt, minus a 34 pt bottom
  band for the labels). So an opaque `CGImage` P3.3 drops on `contents` does **not** hide the title
  strip, and it letterboxes via `kCAGravityResizeAspect`. **P3.2/P3.3 should assume this geometry** —
  the layer is the thumbnail area, and the renderer draws the text band itself. If P3.2's layout wants
  a different split, the constant lives in `panel.m` (`kLabelStrip` / `kTilePad`) and this is the
  coordination point.
- **Implicit CA animations are disabled on the populate path.** `panel_populate` wraps the layer
  add/remove/reframe in a `CATransaction` with `setDisableActions:YES`; without it every keystroke
  would animate the whole strip sliding over 0.25 s.
- **New link dependency: QuartzCore.** `panel.go` adds `#cgo LDFLAGS: -framework QuartzCore` (Core
  Animation: `CALayer`, `CATransaction`). `shim.go` owns the base framework list; this follows
  `capture.go`'s precedent of a file declaring the framework only it needs. The skeleton already used
  `CALayer` but was never link-tested (`go test` does not link a package with no `_test.go`). Verified
  by `go build ./...` and a full `./scripts/build.sh` (universal, minos 12.0 intact).
- **`gt_panel_set_material(GT_MATERIAL_NONE)`** sets the effect view to
  `NSVisualEffectStateInactive` (there is no true "no material") and lets `GTTileView` paint
  `panel_bg` over it. A palette with a translucent `panel_bg` will therefore composite over a dim
  vibrancy tint rather than the raw desktop; finer control is P3.4's from `theme.m`.
- **`panel.go` truncation is now rune-boundary** (was a raw byte cut), matching `shim.m`'s
  `copy_cfstring` — a clipped title stays valid UTF-8 instead of a trailing partial sequence.
- **Verification screenshots** were in-process renders (`/tmp/p31_*_view.png` during the run, not
  kept). They showed: the styled dark slab, four tiles, the blue selection fill + ring moving from
  tile 2 to tile 4 under `gt_panel_update`, truncated CJK/emoji titles, per-tile placeholders, and a
  red test image appearing on tile 0 via `gt_panel_tile_layer(0).contents` with no re-`show`.

### For the integrator / human

- **A window-server screenshot of the live panel was not possible from here.** `screencapture` fails
  with "could not create image from display" — the process is in an Aqua session but the responsible
  process lacks the Screen Recording grant (AGENTS.md §5), which an agent cannot grant. A human should
  drive a `package main` (CreatePanel → ShowPanel → `[NSApp run]`) and confirm on a real display: the
  panel appears centred on the screen **under the mouse** (multi-display: V6.2 territory), over a
  full-screen app, and the app behind stays frontmost. The in-process render verifies the *drawing*;
  it cannot verify compositing, vibrancy, window level, or `collectionBehavior`.
- **`QuartzCore` LDFLAGS** landed in `panel.go`; if the framework list is ever consolidated into
  `shim.go`, fold it in there.
